title: Robot Logic Truth Table
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Flip two robot conditions, pick an and, or, or not rule, and watch the Emergency stop lamp and a live truth table show exactly when the robot stops.

educational.topic: Logical operators and truth tables for robot conditions
learningObjectives: Evaluate and, or, and not expressions for two robot conditions
Apply operator precedence: not first, then and, then or
Complete a truth table by predicting each row
Choose the logical rule that matches a described robot behavior

controls.label: Test my prediction
controls.purpose: Pick a hidden cell and predict True or False

controls.label: True / False
controls.purpose: Submit a prediction for the chosen cell

controls.label: Switches and table rows
controls.purpose: Flip a switch or jump to a row

simulationModel.modelType: Boolean expression evaluator with a truth table
equations: A and B is True only when both are True
A or B is True when at least one is True
not A flips A; not A and B means (not A) and B
assumptions: obstacle_close is True when the distance is under 20 cm
The lamp shows whether the chosen rule would trigger an emergency stop
limitations: Only two inputs and five fixed rules are included

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Prediction practice on an exhaustive truth table
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Switches and rule selector with a live lamp, code line, and hidden-row predictions
keyQuestions: With A or B, which row keeps the lamp dark?
Why is not A and B the same as (not A) and B?
Which rule stops the robot only when it is moving and not close to an obstacle?
How many rows does a truth table with two inputs need?
commonMisconceptions: or means exactly one, not at least one
not A and B means not (A and B)
Checking one example proves a rule is right
assessmentOpportunities: Prediction accuracy in Test my prediction mode
Challenge: dark row is False, False; the rule is not A and B
Exit ticket: full truth table for not A or B
